ecosystemChains.description: Deep snow -> deer yard near farms -> wolf pack follows -> 2-4 livestock incidents -> egg/pork prices rise (scarcity rule) -> council hires Ralf -> pelts and 50-copper bounties -> pack thins -> spring deer rebound -> more deer at orchard -> bark stripped -> apple yield dips -> Mira's wholesale rises.

Mild spring -> brambleback boom -> fewer ticks -> healthier chickens -> more eggs -> egg price drops (surplus rule) -> Maren gathers more herbs instead -> remedy supply rises -> Sella's prices soften; dispersing young draw foxes -> chicken losses -> coop mending -> Doran sells more nails.

species.behavior: Dawn chorus, scratch and peck within ~30m of the coop, dust-bathe midday, roost at dusk.

breeding.note: Heritage birds: ~0.7 eggs/day/hen in warm months, ~0.2 in winter. Hens hatch 6-10 chicks each spring if allowed.

species.danger: None to people; a rooster can scratch a child.
species.fearAggression: Scatter from sudden movement; roosters spur dogs or small children to defend hens.
species.name: Chicken

population.note: 12 hens at Alder Farm plus ~8 across other households; 2 roosters.

taming.note: Individual bonding. Lida's speckled hen is the prototype's bonding tutorial.

species.temperament: Placid, curious; the pecking order is real.

species.behavior: Domestic: fed twice daily, wallow midday, sleep in piles. Boars: nocturnal, solitary males, sounders by day in thickets.

breeding.note: Heritage sows average 6-8 piglets. Village keeps 2-4, slaughters the rest in autumn (the ~200 pork cuts).

species.danger: Domestic: low (a startled 100kg sow shoves). Wild boar: medium - sows with piglets charge within 15m; lone boars bluff-charge but never pursue far.
species.fearAggression: Boars charge if cornered or with young; domestic pigs shove when startled.
species.name: Pig (domestic) / Boar (wild)

population.note: 2 sows at Alder Farm; ~10 wild boars in the forest fringe.

taming.note: Domestic piglets only. Wild boars are never tameable.

species.temperament: Domestic: placid, intelligent, stubborn. Boar: wary, short-tempered.

species.behavior: Graze dawn and dusk, bed midday in thickets, drink at the river by night; yard up in deep snow.

breeding.note: Does drop 1 fawn each spring; twins rare. Wolves take ~8/year, hunters ~4.

species.danger: Low, except rutting stags (medium, seasonal) and winter crop damage.
species.fearAggression: Flight distance ~30m strangers, ~10m known villagers (gradual per-person habituation). Rutting stags (30 autumn days) charge within 10m.
species.name: Deer

population.note: All the worked forest's browse supports; more would strip saplings bare.

produces.note: Venison counted as meat through the kitchen

taming.note: Fawns only (rescued or winter-habituated). Stags can never be tamed. Never safe near village dogs.

species.temperament: Shy, alert, graceful; habituate slowly to familiar people.

species.behavior: Nocturnal in winter, crepuscular in summer; ranges widely, rests by day in cover; howls on still winter nights.

breeding.note: 3-4 pups each spring; one pack is all the forest's game supports.

species.danger: To livestock: real (2-4 incidents/winter). To people: very low - one remembered traveler incident in living memory.
species.fearAggression: Flight distance 50m+ from humans; a cornered wolf fights; a starving pack may test the palisade in deep winter.
species.name: Wolf

population.note: One pack: alpha pair, yearlings, pups. 2-4 livestock incidents per winter (WORLD.md).

produces.note: 10 copper base; crown bounty 50 in winter

taming.note: Orphaned pups only, and keeping one requires the council's approval (Bram enforces, Elswith witnesses). Betrayal can turn a wolf - and the village will demand it be put down.

species.temperament: Intelligent, cautious, loyal to the pack; avoids humans by preference.

species.art: MISSING ART: rabbit-sized burrowing mammal, moss-green quills, whiskered snout, bright black eyes
species.behavior: Forages at dusk and dawn along fixed rounds (barns and coops like a tiny night watchman), naps midday, grooms quills meticulously.

breeding.note: Small litters, high predation - population stable, not booming.

species.danger: None. A quill ball in a child's hands is a lesson, not an injury.
species.fearAggression: Freezes, then bolts for the burrow; rolls into a quill ball if caught; never bites unless squeezed.
species.name: Brambleback

population.note: ~25 active burrows at the forest edge and field margins; pairs raise 2-3 young each spring.

taming.note: The easiest wild tame - the species that teaches the player how taming works. Its treasury (hoarded shiny things) feeds a small lost-item barter economy among children.

species.temperament: Shy, methodical, vain about its treasury.

tamingRules.crueltyOrStarvation: Trust zeroes and the animal locks for a season - it will not bond again until spring.
tamingRules.gainCap: One meaningful trust gain per animal per day.
tamingRules.skillHook: The Taming skill (D-06) multiplies trust gains and unlocks advanced abilities; exact multipliers are D-06's to set.
